# One Connect: independent integration and verification

You are the integration reviewer, separate from the three implementation agents. Work ONLY inside your integration-review workspace. You may read the sibling patches/, handoffs/, and three implementation workspaces under /private/tmp/one-connect-cursor-Bu9W8J for this project's code/evidence. Do not edit those workspaces or the original repository. Other files/accounts/apps are outside your scope.

A common baseline already passed 133 tests. Three Cursor workers implement (a) workflows/review/merge/decisions, (b) multi-project native/Docker DB, (c) versioned skills/connectors/design artifacts. Their complete changed-file patches and handoffs are in patches/ and handoffs/ next to your workspace. Read all handoffs. Apply each patch to this common baseline with three-way merge (all base Git objects are shared), resolve conflicts deliberately and retain every feature; do not overwrite one whole shared file with another version. Do not include another worker's HANDOFF.md as your own handoff. No original repo commit/publication.

Review behavior against docs/one-connect.md and original Build Prompt for Agent Control Center.txt. Confirm authenticated project routing/isolation, no credential logging/egress, explicit human decisions for outward/cost/production actions, no unsafe repository overwrite, shared actual subscription limits, immutable source/review/skill/design revisions, lazy bounded context, restart durability and truthful evidence. Author must never be sole reviewer. Fix integration defects and concrete security/correctness bugs in this isolated workspace; document substantive fixes and remaining findings with file/line/priority.

Specific coordinator audit points: an official CLI reporting subscription but unknown overage must not auto-dispatch without a durable human confirmation that its account's paid overage is off (the current delegation confirmation is not permission for every future app user). Unknown billing remains blocked. Two projects with the same display name and one Obsidian vault must not overwrite or retrieve each other's generated notes; use stable project identity in owned note namespaces with compatible migration. Do not silently compare model versions across unrelated families. Confirm source redaction covers metadata/file paths as well as bodies, and imported mock HTML cannot fetch remote resources or execute in the dashboard's origin. Verify restart/switch does not cancel another project's active runs or close its terminal unintentionally.

Read the coordinator's concrete review notes at /Users/krishkumarsah/Docs/Projects/Interface/docs/verification/delegation/REVIEW_NOTES.md. These are observations of in-progress code, so reassess them against the final patches and repair confirmed defects. You may read this one project verification document without editing the original checkout.

Runtime/browser checks: TypeScript must execute in Node 24 strip-only mode; passing Vitest/tsc alone does not prove that (avoid enums and parameter properties). Run the actual daemon CLI with the prepared Node 24 runtime, or the installed strip-only Node, against disposable local configuration. For HTML mocks, sandbox plus connect-src is not a complete navigation barrier: verify child-frame links and script-driven location changes cannot send requests outside the approved local preview, and parent-origin/IPC/tool access stays denied. Record any missing real-browser verification honestly rather than passing a string-contains assertion as proof.

Run pnpm typecheck, complete vitest suite, SPDX and license inventory, web build, and appropriate offline Rust checks. Read installed dependencies via supplied links, never alter original node_modules or install packages. If sandbox blocks loopback tests/cache paths, record the exact limitation for the coordinator; do not weaken tests or claim they passed. Generate/update docs for final integrated behavior and a requirement-by-requirement evidence matrix: implemented+tested, implemented+unverified, missing, or blocked. Test fixtures alone cannot prove real subscriptions, production deploys, visual quality or semantic answer quality.

Run final checks directly or capture their actual exit status with pipefail. The implementation workers used some `command | tail/grep` pipelines, which returned exit 0 even for intermediate compiler failures; their later stdout does show fixes, but pipeline exit 0 alone is not verification. Do not use a filtered pipeline's status in NEXT_BATCH_READY.json. Record the complete executed check result and any skipped tests; fixture tests and actual native PTY execution are distinct evidence.

List concrete remaining batches for full completion: OpenCode API harness (metered off), Jev recommendations (paid off), release cockpit with ordered action-bound gates, code-host/CI protection/read-only infra/drift, phone PWA/authenticated remote access/notifications, controlled token-quality benchmarks, native packaging/rendered UX, and the original/new acceptance demos. Do not redefine the full goal around this first batch or claim a completed product. Do not write fake health/test/usage evidence.

Safety: owner confirmed Cursor on-demand OFF. Use this exact subscription model, no paid APIs/fallback, no model downgrade, no new agent processes, no credential/config/account changes, no external integration activation, no image pulls, no publishing/push/deploy/outbound messages or production writes. All mutation stays in this isolated integration copy and disposable fixtures. No new dependencies. A human still controls real actions; an agent recommendation cannot approve them.

Finish INTEGRATION_HANDOFF.md with applied patches, conflicts/fixes, independent findings, exact verification commands/results, complete changed-file list, evidence matrix and prioritized missing work. Also write HANDOFF.md pointing to it. Leave the reviewed code in this integration workspace for coordinator inspection and promotion. If a serious blocker remains, keep the evidence honest and preserve useful work. Do not mark the goal complete.

For the next isolated implementation batch, write NEXT_BATCH_READY.json in your workspace with {"state":"verified","checks":[{"command":"...","exitCode":0}],"unresolvedCriticalFindings":[]} ONLY if all required tests/typecheck/web build/SPDX/license/strip-only Node/offline Rust checks actually passed and no confirmed critical security defect remains. Include the exact executed commands and exit codes. Otherwise write {"state":"needs-coordinator-review","checks":[...],"unresolvedCriticalFindings":[...]} and explain the missing or failed checks in your handoff. This marker only allows further development in isolated copies; it never approves promotion, release, paid usage or external activation. Do not manufacture a passing marker to keep the queue moving.
